cell_types.name: Skeletal muscle (myotubes and satellite-like cells)
cell_types.summary: Multinucleated skeletal myotubes and the PAX7-positive progenitors that sit alongside them, made by walking a pluripotent culture through presomitic mesoderm, somite and dermomyotome. People use them to model Duchenne and other dystrophies, to screen drugs on contractile human fibres, and as a source of transplantable myogenic progenitors.
cell_types.maturation_note: Transgene-free monolayer routes are slow: MYOG-positive myocytes appear around day 10-12 and PAX7-positive progenitors after about two weeks (Al Tanoury 2020), while the Shelton CHIR route needs 40-50 days for MYH-positive myotubes. Replating the day-21 culture into SkGM-2 and then a low-CHIR fusion medium gives millimetre-long striated fibres within about a week. Inducible PAX7 or MYOD1 lines reach myotubes far faster but need a transgene.

morphology.endpoint: Long, aligned, multinucleated fibres with visible cross-striations lying over a bed of smaller mononucleated cells. In good cultures the fibres reach a millimetre or more and twitch spontaneously; unfused reserve cells with small bright nuclei sit between them.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat, tightly packed colonies with sharp edges on Matrigel, Geltrex or vitronectin, typically 40-70% confluent at the start of differentiation.

stages.label: Paraxial/presomitic mesoderm
stages.look: Colony borders break down into a dense, fairly uniform sheet of small cells; proliferation slows noticeably compared with untreated wells.

stages.label: Somite and dermomyotome
stages.look: A packed sheet with three-dimensional clusters and ridges rising out of the monolayer; cells are small and refractile.

stages.label: Myocytes appearing
stages.look: Bipolar, elongated cells become obvious among the flatter background cells and begin to align with each other in patches.

stages.label: Myotubes
stages.look: Broad aligned bundles of multinucleated fibres, often with faint striations, that occasionally contract; mononucleated progenitors persist between the fibres.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone within the first few days; Shelton 2014 report a sharp drop in SOX2/NANOG/OCT4 by day 2 of CHIR99021.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Peaks at day 2 in the CHIR route; Shelton 2014 counted 91 +/- 6% T-positive nuclei at this point.

markers.name: MSGN1
markers.note: Paraxial-specific; distinguishes a true presomitic response from the lateral/cardiac mesoderm you get with BMP4 plus activin A.

markers.name: TBX6
markers.note: Up with MSGN1 at day 2 and down again by day 8.

markers.name: PAX3
markers.note: Shelton 2014 report 58 +/- 10% PAX3-positive cells at day 8 versus 1 +/- 1% in untreated wells.

markers.name: PAX7
markers.note: The satellite-like readout. Shelton 2014: 43 +/- 4% at day 50. Al Tanoury 2020 report roughly 20-25% PAX7-Venus-positive mononucleated cells between days 20 and 30.

markers.name: MYF5
markers.note: One of the myogenic regulatory factors; rises from about day 25 in the Shelton route.

markers.name: MYOD1
markers.note: Commitment marker. Also the transgene used in the Maffioletti/Tedesco inducible route.

markers.name: MYOG
markers.note: Al Tanoury 2020 see MYOG-Venus myocytes from day 10, peaking at 12-15% of mononucleated cells at three weeks.

markers.name: MYH3
markers.note: Embryonic isoform dominates in vitro; mature adult isoforms stay low without extra stimulation.

markers.name: MYH1
markers.alias: fast skeletal myosin heavy chain (MY-32 antigen)
markers.note: MF20 and MY-32 pan/fast myosin antibodies are the usual fibre stain; Shelton 2014 report 47 +/- 3% MYH-positive cells at day 50.

markers.name: DES
markers.note: Broad muscle cytoskeletal marker; useful when myosin staining is still weak.

markers.name: NKX2-5
markers.note: Should be low. BMP4 plus activin A instead of CHIR drives cardiac rather than skeletal muscle (Shelton 2014).

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Low levels of neural crest transcripts appear early in the CHIR monolayer route; worth checking if yields are poor.

functional_assays: Spontaneous twitch contraction by phase-contrast or video microscopy
Electrical or optical pacing of myotube contraction
Calcium transients on stimulation
Fusion index from multinucleated MYH-positive fibres
Engraftment and DYSTROPHIN restoration in dystrophic mouse muscle
qc: TBXT-positive nuclei > 85% at day 2 in the CHIR route (Shelton 2014 report 91 +/- 6%)
PAX3-positive cells well above background at day 8 (58 +/- 10% in Shelton 2014)
PAX7-positive plus MYH-positive cells together around 90% of the day-50 culture in the Shelton route
Myotubes multinucleated and striated by immunofluorescence, not just elongated

protocols.name: Chal/Pourquie serum-free route via presomitic mesoderm, with replating for long fibres
protocols.principle: Mimic the embryo: switch Wnt on and BMP off to hold cells in a presomitic state, then let them run forward through somite and dermomyotome to myogenic cells without any transgene or cell sorting. Replating the primary culture into a myoblast growth medium and then a low-CHIR fusion medium produces long striated fibres.

source.authors: Al Tanoury Z, Rao J, Tassy O, Gobert B, et al.
source.title: Differentiation of the human PAX7-positive myogenic precursors/satellite cell lineage in vitro

protocols.efficiency: About 20-25% PAX7-Venus+ and 12-15% MYOG-Venus+ mononucleated cells at 3 weeks; roughly 30% of the culture myogenic (PAX7+ or MYOG+) at 3-4 weeks
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs on Matrigel or Geltrex in a defined maintenance medium, passaged as small clumps and differentiated as a subconfluent monolayer. Al Tanoury 2020 used NCRM1 and PAX7-Venus/MYOG-Venus reporter iPSC lines.

stages.name: Primary myogenic differentiation
stages.base_medium: Serum-free medium as in Chal et al. 2016 (Nat Protoc)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt on, drives presomitic mesoderm

factors.name: LDN193189
factors.role: BMP type I receptor inhibitor; blocks lateral mesoderm

factors.name: FGF2
factors.role: added after the early phase to support progenitor expansion

factors.name: HGF
factors.role: myogenic progenitor support in the later primary phase

factors.name: Knockout serum replacement
factors.role: serum-free protein supplement in the late primary medium

stages.feeding: Daily to every-other-day medium changes over three weeks
actions: Start from a subconfluent feeder-free monolayer
Apply the Chal 2016 sequence of Wnt activation with BMP inhibition, then FGF2, then HGF/IGF-containing medium
Watch for the first MYOG-positive myocytes around day 10-12 and PAX7-positive cells after about two weeks
Do not sort: the protocol is designed to work on the bulk culture
stages.checkpoint: Mononucleated PAX7-positive cells present and small myocytes visible by about day 14-21

stages.name: Replating and progenitor expansion
stages.base_medium: SkGM-2 skeletal muscle growth medium (Lonza CC-3245)

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; for the first 24 h after replating only

stages.feeding: ROCK inhibitor for 24 h, then SkGM-2 alone for 1-2 days
actions: Dissociate the three-week primary culture and filter to remove aggregates
Replate in SkGM-2 with ROCK inhibitor for 24 h
Switch to SkGM-2 without ROCK inhibitor and grow to about 90% confluence
stages.checkpoint: Culture about 90% confluent before fusion is triggered

stages.name: Secondary differentiation (fusion)
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with 2% knockout serum replacement and 1x ITS

factors.name: DAPT
factors.role: optional Notch inhibitor, added for one week to push differentiation

stages.feeding: Change on days 1 and 2, then every other day for about a week
actions: Switch the confluent SkGM-2 culture to the KSR/CHIR fusion medium
Expect fusion to start after about two days
Keep for about a week to obtain millimetre-long striated fibres
Add DAPT only if you want to push differentiation at the expense of the progenitor pool
stages.checkpoint: Striated multinucleated fibres over 1 mm long by immunofluorescence for fast myosin

tips: The primary three-week phase is where most failures happen; check for PAX7 and MYOG by immunofluorescence before committing to replating.
Replating is what produces long fibres: primary cultures alone give short, poorly aligned myotubes.
Reporter lines (PAX7-Venus, MYOG-Venus) make the protocol far easier to troubleshoot, though they are not required.
pitfalls: The PAX7-positive fraction declines after three weeks, so time the replating rather than letting primary cultures run on.
Myogenic yield is only around 30% of the culture even in a good run; the rest is non-myogenic mesoderm.
DAPT shifts the balance towards differentiation and will deplete the satellite-like pool.
unverified: Concentrations and exact day boundaries of CHIR99021, LDN193189, FGF2, HGF and IGF1 in the primary phase: these live in Chal et al. 2016 Nat Protoc (PMID 27583644), which is not open access and could not be read in this session.
Basal medium formulation for the primary phase (Chal 2016) not verified.

protocols.name: Two-day CHIR99021 pulse, then FGF2 and N2 (serum-free, transgene-free)
protocols.principle: A short, strong GSK3-inhibitor pulse pushes almost the whole monolayer into paraxial mesoderm; FGF2 then expands the PAX3/PAX7 progenitor pool while holding back the myogenic regulatory factors, and an N2 medium finally lets the cells commit and fuse.

source.authors: Shelton M, Metz J, Liu J, Carpenedo RL, et al.
source.title: Derivation and expansion of PAX7-positive muscle progenitors from human and mouse embryonic stem cells

protocols.efficiency: 91 +/- 6% TBXT+ at day 2; 58 +/- 10% PAX3+ at day 8; at day 50, 43 +/- 4% PAX7+ and 47 +/- 3% MYH+ (about 90% myogenic)
protocols.start_requirements: H9 hESCs maintained feeder-free on Matrigel in E8. Plate 1.5 x 10^5 cells per well of a Matrigel-coated 12-well plate in E8 with 10 uM Y-27632 overnight before starting. Seeding density is critical: below 1 x 10^5 cells/ml survival drops even with ROCK inhibitor.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.feeding: Daily medium change; 0.1% DMSO is the vehicle control
actions: Replace overnight E8 with E6 plus 10 uM CHIR99021
Keep for exactly 2 days: longer or weaker (2.5 uM) treatment gave less paraxial mesoderm
Change medium daily
stages.checkpoint: TBXT-positive nuclei around 90% at day 2; cells look visibly different from vehicle controls

stages.name: Spontaneous somite/dermomyotome progression
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Wash out CHIR99021 at day 2
Culture in plain E6 and watch for three-dimensional cell clusters by day 8
stages.checkpoint: PAX3-positive cells around 58% at day 8 and visible 3D clusters

stages.name: Progenitor expansion
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Switch to StemPro-34 for days 12-20 to expand the PAX3/PAX7 progenitor pool while suppressing early myogenic regulatory factors
stages.checkpoint: Dense culture with a growing mononucleated progenitor population

stages.name: Return to basal medium
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Return to E6 from day 20 to day 35
stages.checkpoint: PAX7, MYF5, MYOD1 and MYOG transcripts clearly up by day 25

stages.name: Terminal differentiation
stages.feeding: Daily medium change
actions: Switch to N2 medium at day 35
Expect the first myocytes about 5 days later (day 40)
Hold to day 50 for large aligned myocyte/myotube fields
stages.checkpoint: 47 +/- 3% MYH-positive cells and 43 +/- 4% PAX7-positive cells at day 50; spontaneous contractions visible

materials: Antibodies to TBXT, PAX3, PAX7, MF20
tips: Ten micromolar CHIR99021 for exactly two days beat both 2.5 uM and longer exposures in the authors' titration.
Total cell number grows about 20-fold from day 0 to day 50, and about 42% of day-50 PAX7-positive cells still incorporate EdU, so the progenitor pool is genuinely proliferative.
Forskolin, which helps in aggregate-based protocols, gave no extra benefit in this monolayer system.
pitfalls: Seeding density is the single most important variable; sparse wells die or differentiate off-target.
BMP4 plus activin A instead of CHIR gives cardiac, not skeletal, muscle.
Low levels of neural crest transcripts are present early and about 10% of the day-50 culture is neither PAX7+ nor MYH+.

protocols.name: Four-day somite induction, then CHIR/FGF2 and an HGF/IGF1 fusion medium
protocols.principle: Build a somite stage first with a CHIR pulse followed by dual BMP and TGF-beta inhibition, then take the somite cells towards myogenic fate with CHIR plus FGF2 and finish in a KSR medium with HGF and IGF1. Day-29 cells can be dissociated, expanded in SkGM-2 and refused in N2 medium.

source.authors: Xi H, Fujiwara W, Gonzalez K, Jan M, et al.
source.title: In Vivo Human Somitogenesis Guides Somite Development from hPSCs

protocols.start_requirements: On day -1 dissociate hPSC colonies to single cells with TrypLE Express and seed on Matrigel-coated plates at 25,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632.

stages.name: Paraxial mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: BDM: DMEM/F12 with 1% ITS-G and 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Switch mTeSR1 to BDM plus 3 uM CHIR99021 on day 0
Feed daily for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: TBX6-positive paraxial mesoderm by immunofluorescence/flow

stages.name: Somite specification
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Replace the CHIR medium with BDM plus LDN193189 and SB431542 for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: Somite-stage culture at day 4, PDGFRA+/KDR- by flow

stages.name: Myogenic commitment

factors.name: FGF2
factors.role: supports survival of the dense culture

stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: On day 4 switch to BDM with 3 uM CHIR99021 and 20 ng/ml FGF2 for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: Dense culture surviving the transition without large gaps

stages.name: Myotube differentiation
stages.base_medium: DMEM with 15% knockout serum replacement and 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin
stages.feeding: Every other day after day 6
actions: Switch to the KSR/HGF/IGF1 medium on day 6
Keep for 14-21 days, feeding every other day
stages.checkpoint: Myogenic markers by immunofluorescence at day 27

stages.name: Optional replating and fusion
stages.base_medium: SkGM-2 then N2 medium (BDM with 1% N2 supplement)
stages.feeding: SkGM-2 plus FGF2 for 7-10 days, then N2 medium for 5 days
actions: At day 29 dissociate with collagenase IV then TrypLE, filter through 100 um and 40 um strainers
Replate at 15,000-20,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel in SkGM-2 plus 20 ng/ml FGF2
Grow 7-10 days to over 70% confluence, then switch to N2 medium for 5 days to trigger fusion
stages.checkpoint: Fused multinucleated myotubes after 5 days in N2 medium

tips: The same first four days feed the authors' osteogenic and chondrogenic routes, so one somite induction can be split three ways.
FGF2 at the day 4-6 step is there for survival of a very dense culture, not for patterning.
The N2 fusion step is taken from Shelton 2014 and works on replated, expanded progenitors.
pitfalls: Seeding at day -1 must give an even monolayer; patchy wells differentiate unevenly.
The paper reports marker dynamics rather than a single purity figure, so set your own acceptance threshold on TBX6 and PDGFRA.
unverified: No overall myogenic purity percentage is given for the day-27 or replated cultures in this paper.

cell_types.notes: Three families of protocol exist and they are not interchangeable. Transgene-free monolayer routes (Chal/Pourquie, Shelton, Xi) need 4-7 weeks and top out around 30-90% myogenic depending on how you count, but need no genetic modification. Inducible-transgene routes are much faster and cleaner: Darabi et al. 2012 (Cell Stem Cell, PMID 22560081) differentiate doxycycline-inducible PAX7 hES/hiPSC lines for 7 days as embryoid bodies, replate for 3 days, induce PAX7 with doxycycline on day 10, sort GFP+ cells after 4 days of induction and expand them in bFGF plus doxycycline; Maffioletti et al. 2015 (Nat Protoc, PMID 26042384; corrigendum PMID 26313482) derive mesoangioblast-like cells in four density/medium/coating stages and then induce MYOD1 transiently. Both require a vector and a sort. Lines differ substantially in how they respond to the CHIR dose and in how long they take to reach myotubes, so titrate CHIR and re-time the stages for each new line.

cell_types.name: Mesenchymal stromal cells (iMSC)
cell_types.summary: Fibroblast-like, plastic-adherent cells that carry the standard MSC surface signature (CD73, CD90, CD105 positive, CD45 negative) and differentiate to bone, cartilage and fat. The iPSC-derived version gives an inexhaustible, donor-matched substitute for bone-marrow MSCs for regenerative and immunomodulation studies, and is the usual starting material for osteogenic, chondrogenic and adipogenic assays.
cell_types.maturation_note: Surface markers appear fast but the population only becomes stable with passaging: Fukuta 2014 saw CD73/CD105/CD44 rise within 48 h of the medium switch and the transition from neural crest to MSC complete by about passage 3, while Chen 2012 reach a stable MSC-like culture at roughly 20 days. Trilineage potential should be re-checked every few passages.

morphology.endpoint: A confluent lawn of flat, spindle-shaped, fibroblast-like cells with a whorled or parallel arrangement at high density, indistinguishable by eye from bone-marrow MSCs.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies with defined edges on Matrigel or laminin in a defined maintenance medium.

stages.label: Intermediate (neural crest or mesendoderm)
stages.look: Cells migrate out of the colonies as a dense, cuboidal sheet; in the neural crest route the outgrowth is p75/TFAP2A positive while cells still inside the colony stay PAX6 positive.

stages.label: Early MSC-like cells
stages.look: Cells elongate and lose the tight epithelial packing; morphology changes noticeably about 4 days after the medium switch.

stages.label: Expanded iMSC
stages.look: Uniform spindle-shaped fibroblast-like monolayer that tolerates weekly trypsin passaging at low density.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be lost. Fukuta 2014 found pluripotency transcripts below detection and no SSEA4-positive cells in the final iMSCs.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Residual expression means residual undifferentiated cells and teratoma risk.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: The sorting gate in the Fukuta route: about 35-41% p75-high cells after 7 days with SB431542 plus CHIR99021. Falls within 48 h of the MSC medium switch.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Neural crest identity; drops rapidly once MSC medium is applied.

markers.name: TFAP2A
markers.note: Marks the migratory outgrowth; declines gradually to passage 3.

markers.name: NT5E
markers.note: Core ISCT positive marker; rises within 48 h of the switch to MSC medium in Fukuta 2014.

markers.name: ENG
markers.note: Core ISCT positive marker; reaches bone-marrow-MSC levels by about passage 2.

markers.name: THY1
markers.note: Core ISCT positive marker, reported for the Chen 2012 iMSCs.

markers.name: CD44
markers.note: Routinely included in the iMSC panel in both routes.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: Must be negative; the ISCT definition requires absence of haematopoietic markers.

markers.name: PECAM1
markers.note: Should be absent; Chen 2012 report CD31-negative iMSCs.

markers.name: RUNX2
markers.note: Read out after osteogenic challenge, not in the undifferentiated iMSC.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Read out after chondrogenic pellet or micromass challenge.

markers.name: PPARG
markers.note: Read out after adipogenic challenge; iPSC-derived MSCs are often poorly adipogenic unless TGF-beta is inhibited.

functional_assays: Trilineage differentiation (alizarin red, safranin-O/alcian blue, oil red O)
Plastic adherence and colony-forming unit fibroblast assay
Population doubling and passage stability
Immunomodulation assays, e.g. interferon-gamma-induced HLA expression
In vivo perfusion recovery in hindlimb ischaemia models
qc: CD73, CD90, CD105 and CD44 positive and CD45 negative by flow (ISCT criteria)
No SSEA4-positive cells and pluripotency transcripts below detection before any in vivo use (Fukuta 2014)
Osteogenic, chondrogenic and adipogenic differentiation demonstrated after derivation
Normal karyotype after expansion

protocols.name: Single small molecule: 10 days of SB431542, then serum MSC medium
protocols.principle: Blocking TGF-beta/activin signalling for ten days drives a confluent hiPSC culture out of pluripotency and into a mesengenic intermediate; switching to a standard serum MSC medium and passaging at decreasing density then selects a stable MSC-like population.

source.authors: Chen YS, Pelekanos RA, Ellis RL, Horne R, et al.
source.title: Small molecule mesengenic induction of human induced pluripotent stem cells to generate mesenchymal stem/stromal cells

protocols.efficiency: 96% of day-10 SB431542-treated cells were EpCAM-negative/NCAM-positive; the final MSC-like cells are reported as marker-positive without a stated percentage
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs grown in mTeSR1 on Matrigel-coated vessels (Matrigel at 100 ug/ml in DMEM/Ham's F-12, 1 h at room temperature) and allowed to reach confluence before induction.

stages.name: Mesengenic induction
stages.base_medium: KOSR medium without bFGF: DMEM/Ham's F-12 with 20% knockout serum replacement, 1 mM L-glutamine, 10 mM non-essential amino acids

factors.name: SB431542
factors.role: TGF-beta/activin receptor inhibitor; drives exit from pluripotency towards mesenchyme

stages.feeding: KOSR plus SB431542 replaced daily for 10 days
actions: Grow hiPSCs to confluence in mTeSR1 on Matrigel
Switch to KOSR without bFGF plus 10 uM SB431542
Replace the medium daily for 10 days
At day 10 passage as single cells with TrypLE Select
stages.checkpoint: About 96% EpCAM-negative/NCAM-positive cells at day 10; CD73 and CD105 still largely negative at this point

stages.name: MSC selection and expansion
stages.base_medium: DMEM high glucose with 10% non-heat-inactivated fetal calf serum, 2 mM L-glutamine, 50 U/ml penicillin-streptomycin, 20 ug/ml gentamicin
stages.feeding: Routine MSC feeding with passaging at decreasing seeding density
actions: Seed the day-10 cells (MP0) at 40,000 cells/cm2 in MSC medium
Seed MP1 at 20,000 cells/cm2
Seed later passages at 10,000 cells/cm2
Continue to about day 20, by which point the culture is MSC-like
stages.checkpoint: By passage 6 the cells express CD73, CD90, CD105, CD29, CD44 and CD146 and lack CD45, CD34, CD14, CD11b, HLA-DR, CD31 and CD117

tips: The protocol needs only one small molecule, which makes it the cheapest route to iMSCs.
Stepping the seeding density down with each passage is part of the selection, not an afterthought.
Expect CD73/CD105 to appear only after the switch to serum MSC medium, not during SB431542 treatment.
pitfalls: Serum-containing MSC medium makes this route less suitable for clinical translation than defined alternatives.
The paper gives marker positivity qualitatively; set your own purity gate.
Non-heat-inactivated serum is specified; lot-to-lot serum variation is a real source of failure.
unverified: Final percentage purity for CD73/CD90/CD105/CD45 in the MSC-like population is not stated in the paper.
The Results section describes the MSC medium as DMEM-HG plus 10% fetal bovine serum while the Methods specify fetal calf serum with gentamicin; the discrepancy is in the source.

protocols.name: Via neural crest: SB431542 plus CHIR99021 in chemically defined medium, then MSC medium
protocols.principle: Cranial neural crest is a physiological source of mesenchymal cells for the craniofacial skeleton. Inhibiting TGF-beta while weakly activating Wnt in a chemically defined medium produces p75-high neural crest cells in 7 days; those cells convert to MSCs over about three passages in MSC medium. Everything can be done xeno-free.

source.authors: Fukuta M, Nakai Y, Kirino K, Nakagawa M, et al.
source.title: Derivation of mesenchymal stromal cells from pluripotent stem cells through a neural crest lineage using small molecule compounds with defined media

protocols.efficiency: About 35% p75-high cells with SB431542 alone, rising with 1 uM CHIR99021; 40.9 +/- 5.5% under the fully xeno-free StemFit/iMatrix conditions
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs transferred to feeder-free culture: dissociate colonies into clumps of about 10 cells, seed on Matrigel-coated dishes at 2-4 clumps/cm2 and culture in mTeSR1 for 2 days. For the xeno-free version, seed single cells on iMatrix-coated dishes in StemFit and culture 5 days.

stages.name: Neural crest induction
stages.base_medium: Chemically defined medium (CDM): IMDM/Ham's F-12 1:1, 1x chemically defined lipid concentrate, 15 ug/ml apo-transferrin, 450 uM monothioglycerol, 5 mg/ml purified BSA, 7 ug/ml insulin, penicillin-streptomycin

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt activation, dose-dependent up to 1 uM only

stages.feeding: CDM with both compounds, refreshed through the 7-day induction
actions: Replace mTeSR1 (or StemFit) with CDM plus 10 uM SB431542 and 1 uM CHIR99021
Let cells migrate out of the colonies over 7 days (7-10 days under xeno-free conditions)
Harvest and sort on p75 (NGFR) expression to isolate the p75-high fraction, or carry the bulk culture forward
stages.checkpoint: p75-high fraction around 35-41% by flow; outgrowing cells stain for p75 and TFAP2A while cells left in colonies are PAX6-positive

stages.name: Optional neural crest expansion
stages.feeding: CDM with SB431542, EGF and FGF2
actions: If you need more cells, expand the sorted neural crest cells in CDM with SB431542, EGF and FGF2 rather than the induction medium, which supports very poor growth
Stable expansion was shown over 10 passages with retained TFAP2A expression
stages.checkpoint: Expanded cells keep neural crest morphology and global expression profile (r = 0.96-0.98 versus passage 0)

stages.name: MSC induction and passaging
stages.base_medium: Alpha-MEM with 10% fetal bovine serum (or, xeno-free, STK2 MSC medium on fibronectin-coated dishes)
stages.feeding: Weekly passaging with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA at 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2
actions: Plate neural crest cells at 6.5 x 10^4 cells/cm2 in CDM with 10 uM SB431542 and 1 uM CHIR99021
The next day switch to alpha-MEM plus 10% FBS (or STK2 for defined conditions)
Expect the morphology to change about 4 days later
Passage weekly at 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2; analyse MSC markers 14 days after induction
stages.checkpoint: CD73, CD105 and CD44 positive and CD45 negative by flow; cuboidal morphology becomes fibroblastic by about passage 3

tips: CHIR99021 helps only up to 1 uM; higher doses sharply reduce the p75-high fraction.
The protocol is deliberately BMP-independent: adding BMP4 inhibits induction, but so do BMP inhibitors (DMH1, LDN193189, Noggin), so leave BMP signalling alone.
The whole route, including osteogenic induction with STK3, can be run under chemically defined xeno-free conditions.
pitfalls: Seeding density changes the balance between central nervous system and neural crest fate; follow the stated clump and cell densities.
Neural crest cells grow very slowly in the induction medium itself; move them to the EGF/FGF2 medium if you need numbers.
The transition from neural crest to MSC takes until about passage 3, so do not judge marker profiles too early.

protocols.name: Clonal iMSC lines isolated by CD24-negative/CD105-positive sorting
protocols.principle: Differentiate hiPSCs under a clinically compliant protocol and then purify MSC-like cells by sorting out the CD24-negative, CD105-positive fraction, so the resulting lines are monoclonal and karyotypically stable.

source.authors: Lian Q, Zhang Y, Zhang J, Zhang HK, et al.
source.title: Functional mesenchymal stem cells derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells attenuate limb ischemia in mice

protocols.efficiency: Three monoclonal, karyotypically stable, functional MSC-like cultures were isolated
protocols.start_requirements: Human iPSCs differentiated under what the authors describe as a clinically compliant protocol; the starting culture conditions are not stated in the abstract.

stages.name: MSC differentiation
actions: Induce MSC differentiation from hiPSCs under the authors' clinically compliant protocol
stages.checkpoint: Loss of pluripotency-associated markers

stages.name: Sorting and clonal expansion
actions: Sort cells on CD24-negative and CD105-positive expression
Expand sorted cells as monoclonal lines
Confirm MSC surface antigens, absence of pluripotency markers and trilineage differentiation
stages.checkpoint: MSC surface antigen profile with adipocyte, osteocyte and chondrocyte differentiation and a normal karyotype

materials: Anti-CD24 and anti-CD105 antibodies for FACS
tips: The CD24-negative/CD105-positive gate is the distinctive part of this protocol and is worth borrowing even on top of other induction routes.
The authors report these iMSCs outperform adult bone-marrow MSCs in a hindlimb ischaemia model, attributed to better survival and engraftment.
A later Methods in Molecular Biology chapter from the same group (Lian et al. 2016, PMID 27236679) sets out the directed differentiation in protocol form.
pitfalls: Clonal derivation means line-to-line variation between clones; characterise each clone separately.
Without the full methods, timings and media here have to be taken from the primary paper.
unverified: Stage durations, base media, growth factor concentrations and seeding densities: the Circulation paper is not open access and only the abstract could be read in this session.
Day boundaries for both stages are unknown (set to null).

cell_types.notes: Beware of what 'iMSC' means in a given paper: the ISCT surface panel is easy to satisfy and tells you very little about origin or potency. The three routes here arrive at the same flow profile through different embryology (TGF-beta-blocked mesenchyme, cranial neural crest, or sorted CD24-/CD105+ clones), and their differentiation biases differ accordingly. iPSC-derived MSCs are notoriously poorly adipogenic compared with bone-marrow MSCs; Su et al. 2018 overcome this by adding the TGF-beta inhibitor SB431542 during adipogenic induction. Re-test trilineage potential and karyotype every few passages, and confirm the absence of SSEA4-positive cells and pluripotency transcripts before any transplantation experiment.

cell_types.name: Chondrocytes (cartilage)
cell_types.summary: SOX9-positive cells that deposit a proteoglycan-rich, collagen type II matrix, grown as three-dimensional pellets or micromasses after a staged monolayer induction through paraxial mesoderm and sclerotome. They are used to model osteoarthritis and skeletal dysplasias, to test cartilage-protective drugs, and as a renewable source for cartilage repair.
cell_types.maturation_note: The monolayer induction takes 12-21 days, then pellets or micromasses need 28-42 days more before the matrix is convincing. Safranin-O staining and GAG/DNA ratios keep rising to about day 42. Keeping TGF-beta3 gives articular-like cartilage, while switching to BMP4 pushes the tissue towards hypertrophy and endochondral ossification.

morphology.endpoint: A dense, glossy, cartilage-like pellet or micromass a millimetre or so across, firm enough to handle with forceps, with rounded cells sitting in lacunae in a matrix that stains strongly with safranin-O. Off-target cells, when present, appear as a looser perichondral rim.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat compact colonies on vitronectin or Matrigel; the Adkar/Wu route starts at only 40-70% confluence.

stages.label: Paraxial mesoderm and early somite
stages.look: Dense, uniform monolayer with no visible colony boundaries after the daily medium swaps.

stages.label: Sclerotome
stages.look: Confluent sheet that becomes more refractile; cells are smaller and tightly apposed.

stages.label: Chondroprogenitors
stages.look: A mixed monolayer of flattened and spindle-shaped cells ready to be dissociated and pelleted.

stages.label: Chondrogenic pellet
stages.look: Opaque, rounded pellet that holds its shape; cut sections show rounded cells in a safranin-O-positive matrix.

stages.label: Mature cartilage
stages.look: Larger, firmer, whiter tissue with an even matrix; perichondral off-target layers are reduced when WNT is inhibited.

markers.name: TBXT

markers.name: TBX6

markers.name: SOX9

markers.name: COL2A1

protocols.name: Daily-stepped sclerotome induction, then TGF-beta3 pellet chondrogenesis (COL2A1-GFP sortable)
protocols.principle: Follow the embryonic sequence one day at a time (anterior primitive streak, paraxial mesoderm, early somite, sclerotome, chondroprogenitor), each stage defined by a specific set of agonists and antagonists, then pellet the chondroprogenitors in TGF-beta3. A CRISPR COL2A1-GFP reporter lets you sort the chondrogenic cells.

source.title: Step-wise chondrogenesis of human induced pluripotent stem cells and purification via a reporter allele generated by CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing

Feed the paraxial cocktail for 24 h

factors.name: PD173074

stages.base_medium: Chondrogenic medium: DMEM/F-12 GlutaMAX with 1% FBS, 1% ITS+, 55 uM 2-mercaptoethanol, 1% MEM non-essential amino acids, 1% penicillin-streptomycin

factors.name: TGF-beta3
factors.role: chondrogenic driver; favours articular over hypertrophic fate

Centrifuge 5 min at 300 x g, resuspend in chondrogenic medium

Culture 28 days, changing medium every 3 days

The COL2A1-GFP reporter is the most reliable way to compare runs, since SOX9 immunostaining does not track matrix quality.
pitfalls: Pellets from late-passage (P3-P5) progenitors show more type I collagen and less type II.
Starting the induction at the wrong confluence (not around 70%) is a common cause of failure.

protocols.name: Same staged induction with WNT (and optionally MITF) inhibition through pellet culture

Adding the porcupine inhibitor Wnt-C59 (and optionally the MITF inhibitor ML329) throughout pellet culture suppresses those off-target populations and gives a more homogeneous cartilage.

Dissociate with TrypLE for 3 min at 37 C and neutralise with DMEM/F12 plus 10% FBS

stages.base_medium: Chondrogenic medium: DMEM/F-12 with 1% FBS, 1% ITS+, 55 uM 2-mercaptoethanol, 100 nM dexamethasone, 1% NEAA, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 50 ug/ml L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, 40 ug/ml L-proline

factors.role: porcupine inhibitor; suppresses neural and melanocytic off-target cells, applied day 0 to day 42 of pellet culture

factors.name: ML329
factors.role: MITF inhibitor; optional, used alone or with C59 to suppress melanocyte-like cells

Centrifuge 5 min at 300 x g to form pellets
Add TGF-beta3 with 1 uM C59 (and 1 uM ML329 if desired) from pellet day 0 through day 42
Score safranin-O staining and off-target cells on sections

tips: WNT inhibition during pellet culture (not during the somite step, where WNT is required) is the key change relative to the parent protocol.
RNA-FISH showed WNT ligands concentrated in the perichondral layer, which explains why the off-target cells sit at the pellet rim.
The published scRNA-seq atlas across hiPSC, sclerotome, Cp and six pellet time points is a useful reference dataset for benchmarking your own cultures.
pitfalls: Timing matters: inhibiting WNT during somite specification blocks the protocol, so apply C59 only in pellet culture.
MITF inhibition alone is less effective than WNT inhibition; the two were tested in combination.
The paper reports qualitative improvement rather than a purity number, so define your own histology score before you start.

protocols.name: Craft/Keller embryoid-body route to articular chondrocytes in high-density micromass

factors.role: articular chondrocyte fate; added from day 3 of micromass culture

factors.name: BMP4

cell_types.notes: Two protocol families dominate: monolayer sclerotome routes (Loh-derived; Adkar 2019, Wu 2021) and embryoid-body routes (Oldershaw/Kimber and Craft/Keller). The landmark Oldershaw et al. 2010 paper (Nat Biotechnol, PMID 20967028) reported a chemically defined 3-stage protocol giving 74% SOX9-positive cells in HUES1 and up to 95-97% in HUES7/HUES8, but it is not open access and its growth factor concentrations and day boundaries could not be verified here; the same group's later open-access work (Cheng et al. 2014, PMID 25273540; Wang et al. 2019, PMID 31326745) builds on it. The articular/hypertrophic distinction is real and matters for any repair application: TGF-beta signalling gives stable articular-like cartilage, BMP4 gives hypertrophic cartilage that ossifies. Off-target neural and melanocytic cells are the main contaminant and are best controlled by WNT inhibition during pellet culture (Wu 2021) or by sorting a COL2A1 reporter (Adkar 2019). Chondroprogenitors can be expanded, but matrix quality falls with passage number.

cell_types.name: Osteoblasts (bone)
cell_types.summary: RUNX2- and SP7-positive bone-forming cells that deposit a collagen type I matrix and mineralise it into alizarin-red-positive nodules. iPSC-derived osteoblasts are used to model skeletal disease (for example fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and other heritable bone disorders), to screen bone-augmentation compounds, and as a cell source for bone tissue engineering.
cell_types.maturation_note: Osteoblast transcripts (RUNX2, SP7) rise within the first week, but mineralisation takes longer: alizarin red and von Kossa staining become clear at days 19-23 in the Kanke/Zujur small-molecule routes, and the StemPro osteogenesis route in Xi 2017 runs for 28 days after the somite stage. Nodules keep mineralising if the culture is held longer.

morphology.endpoint: A dense layer of cuboidal to polygonal cells overlaid by refractile matrix, with dark, three-dimensional mineral nodules visible by phase contrast and strongly alizarin-red positive.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies on vitronectin in a defined medium, taken to about 70% confluence before induction.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Colonies break up under high-dose CHIR99021; cells form clusters and the sheet looks uneven. Substantial cell death at this step is expected.

stages.label: Osteoblast induction
stages.look: Replated cells form a dense proliferating monolayer that begins to look granular.

stages.label: Early mineralisation
stages.look: Small dark nodules appear within cell clusters; alizarin red staining is clearly positive.

stages.label: Mineralised osteoblast layer
stages.look: Confluent layer with multiple dense mineral nodules, RUNX2 throughout the clusters and SP7 concentrated at their periphery.

markers.name: TBXT

markers.name: MIXL1

markers.name: PDGFRA

markers.name: RUNX2

markers.name: SP7

markers.name: COL1A1
markers.note: Main bone matrix protein; the 2.3 kb Col1a1-GFP reporter is the classic osteoblast reporter in these protocols.

markers.name: ALPL
markers.note: Enzymatic activity stain is the quickest functional osteoblast readout, though it is also high in hPSCs, so use it after pluripotency is lost.

markers.name: IBSP
markers.note: Significantly upregulated at days 19-23 in hiPSCs in Kanke 2014.

markers.name: BGLAP
markers.note: Late mineralisation marker; clearly induced in the mouse arm of Kanke 2014.

markers.name: SPP1
markers.note: Commonly reported alongside IBSP and BGLAP in osteogenic panels.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Should stay low; SOX1/SOX2 induction indicates ectodermal drift, which Zujur 2020 monitored across CHIR doses.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Checked in Zujur 2020 and not significantly altered at any CHIR concentration tested.

markers.name: ACAN
markers.note: Cartilage drift is the usual off-target in sclerotome-derived osteogenic cultures.

protocols.name: Xeno-free small-molecule osteoblasts: CHIR/cyclopamine, then SAG and a helioxanthin derivative
protocols.principle: Three phases with defined small molecules only: activate Wnt and block hedgehog to make mesoderm, then switch hedgehog on with SAG together with the helioxanthin derivative TH to induce osteoblasts, and finally mature the cells in osteogenic medium alone. The whole protocol runs on Essential 8/vitronectin with no Matrigel and no serum.

source.authors: Zujur D, Kanke K, Onodera S, Tani S, et al.
source.title: Stepwise strategy for generating osteoblasts from human pluripotent stem cells under fully defined xeno-free conditions with small-molecule inducers

protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs adapted over 6-10 passages to Essential 8 medium on recombinant human vitronectin-coated dishes (5 ug/ml), grown in 6-well plates to 70% confluence (day 0).

stages.name: Mesoderm induction

actions: Start at 70% confluence on vitronectin

stages.name: Osteoblast induction

factors.name: SAG
factors.role: smoothened agonist; hedgehog on for osteoblast induction

factors.name: TH (helioxanthin derivative)

factors.role: Wnt reactivation to push osteoblast differentiation

stages.base_medium: Xeno-free osteogenic medium with no inducers
stages.feeding: Daily medium change for 9 days
actions: Culture in xeno-free OG medium alone from day 12 to day 21
Stain with alizarin red to confirm mineralisation

The same group also ran the protocol on Cellnest recombinant collagen peptide scaffolds for 3D bone constructs.

cell_types.notes: White, beige and brown are three different products and the route determines which you get. Mesenchymal-progenitor routes (Ahfeldt 2012, Su 2018) give white or beige cells; the paraxial mesoderm route (Zhang 2020) is the one aimed at genuine brown adipocytes, consistent with brown fat and skeletal muscle sharing a progenitor. cell_types.name: Somites / paraxial mesoderm
cell_types.summary: The transient paraxial mesoderm and somite stages that give rise to skeletal muscle, bone, cartilage and dermis, now reproducible in vitro within 3-6 days by timed Wnt, BMP, TGF-beta, FGF and hedgehog manipulation. They are the common starting point for musculoskeletal differentiation and the platform for studying human segmentation clock timing and segmentation disorders.
cell_types.maturation_note: Everything happens fast and the windows are short: Loh 2016 go pluripotent to anterior primitive streak in 24 h, to paraxial mesoderm by day 2, to 96.8 +/- 5.7% FOXC2-positive early somite by day 3, and to sclerotome or dermomyotome by day 5-6. Paraxial markers collapse within 6 hours of FGF/Wnt withdrawal, so stage transitions must be on time to the hour, not the day.

morphology.endpoint: A dense, uniform, almost featureless monolayer of small tightly packed cells: the somite stages have little distinctive morphology, which is exactly why marker checks matter. In 3D somitoid cultures, by contrast, you see a train of regularly spaced epithelial somite-like blocks budding off an elongating aggregate.

For cartilage, take day-6 sclerotome into 20 ng/ml BMP4 for 3-6 days; for fibroblast-like cells, take day-5 sclerotome into 10 ng/ml TGF-beta1 plus 2 ng/ml PDGF-BB for 72 h
stages.checkpoint: 85.2 +/- 8.4% PDGFRA-positive cells expressing FOXC2, PAX1 and PAX9 at day 5-6

stages.name: Dermomyotome (dorsal branch, alternative)

factors.name: Vismodegib
factors.role: hedgehog inhibitor; blocks the sclerotome alternative

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: sometimes added to the dermomyotome condition

actions: Treat day-3 somites with CHIR99021 plus vismodegib (with or without BMP4) for 48 h
stages.checkpoint: Dermomyotome identity at day 5 (the skeletal muscle precursor branch)

tips: The underlying logic is explicit: every step both specifies the wanted fate and blocks the alternative, which is why each cocktail contains inhibitors as well as agonists.
The in vivo clock is 12-24 h per step (epiblast, primitive streak, paraxial mesoderm, early somite, sclerotome), and the in vitro protocol mirrors that, so do not stretch the stages.
DLL1 and PDGFRA give you sortable handles on paraxial mesoderm and sclerotome respectively, which is the cleanest way to remove off-target cells.
pitfalls: Marker transitions happen within hours (paraxial genes fall within 6 h of FGF/Wnt inhibition), so late medium changes blur stage identity.
Getting the primitive streak flavour wrong (anterior versus mid) sends everything downstream to lateral rather than paraxial fate.
Day-6 sclerotome formed ectopic bone in mice over 2-3 months, so these cells are potent; treat transplantation experiments accordingly.
unverified: CDM2 basal medium composition is given in the paper's Supplemental Procedures, which could not be read in this session.

protocols.name: Four-day somite induction benchmarked against human embryo somites
protocols.principle: A two-step, two-medium induction: a CHIR99021 pulse for paraxial mesoderm, then dual BMP and TGF-beta inhibition for somite formation, with the resulting cells compared directly against staged human embryonic somites and then pushed to muscle, bone or cartilage.

source.authors: Xi H, Fujiwara W, Gonzalez K, Jan M, et al.
source.title: In Vivo Human Somitogenesis Guides Somite Development from hPSCs

protocols.efficiency: Reported as TBX6-positive and PDGFRA-positive/KDR-negative fractions with means +/- SEM in figures; no single headline percentage
protocols.start_requirements: On day -1 dissociate hPSC colonies to single cells with TrypLE Express and seed on Matrigel-coated plates at 25,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632.

stages.name: Paraxial mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: BDM: DMEM/F12 with 1% ITS-G and 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Switch mTeSR1 to BDM plus 3 uM CHIR99021 on day 0
Feed daily for 2 days
stages.checkpoint: TBX6-positive paraxial mesoderm by immunofluorescence and flow

stages.name: Somite specification
stages.feeding: Fresh medium daily
actions: Switch to BDM plus LDN193189 and SB431542 for 2 days
Score PDGFRA and KDR by flow at day 4
stages.checkpoint: PDGFRA-positive/KDR-negative somite-stage population at day 4

tips: This four-day block is the shared trunk for the paper's myogenic (CHIR/FGF2 then HGF/IGF1), osteogenic (SAG/FGF2 then StemPro osteogenesis) and chondrogenic (SAG/FGF2 then StemPro chondrogenesis pellet) arms.
PDGFRA-positive/KDR-negative is a quick flow gate separating paraxial from lateral/endothelial mesoderm.
The in vivo benchmarking against staged human somites in the paper is a useful sanity check on your own marker panel.
pitfalls: Only two media are used, so there is little room to correct a drifting culture mid-run; seeding density on day -1 is the main lever.
The protocol does not separate sclerotome from dermomyotome; that happens in the downstream arms.
unverified: No single numeric purity figure for the day-4 somite stage is given in the text.

protocols.name: Presomitic mesoderm, somite and dermomyotome with a PAX3-GFP reporter
protocols.principle: Induce presomitic mesoderm with simultaneous Wnt activation, FGF, TGF-beta inhibition and BMP inhibition, sort DLL1-positive cells, then specify somite with a lower CHIR99021 dose plus TGF-beta inhibition and dermomyotome by adding BMP4. A PAX3-GFP reporter line quantifies each step.

source.authors: Nakajima T, Shibata M, Nishio M, Nagata S, et al.
source.title: Modeling human somite development and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva with induced pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: PAX3-GFP+ somite cells: 52.1 +/- 0.8% with SB431542 alone, 70.7 +/- 0.1% with 5 uM CHIR99021, 74.7 +/- 0.5% with both; only 0.3-0.7% with 10 uM CHIR99021
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs including a PAX3-GFP reporter line, pre-cultured for 3 days before the chemically defined induction begins.

stages.name: Presomitic mesoderm induction

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt on for presomitic mesoderm

stages.feeding: 4 days in CDM with the four factors, after 3 days of pre-culture
actions: Pre-culture for 3 days
Induce presomitic mesoderm for 4 days with CHIR99021, FGF2, SB431542 and DMH1
Sort DLL1-positive presomitic mesoderm cells
stages.checkpoint: DLL1-positive presomitic mesoderm by flow at day 4

stages.name: Somite induction

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: lower-dose Wnt activation; note that 10 uM here abolishes somite induction

stages.feeding: 4 days
actions: Treat sorted DLL1-positive cells with 5 uM CHIR99021 plus 10 uM SB431542 for 4 days
Score PAX3-GFP and DLL1 by flow
stages.checkpoint: 74.7 +/- 0.5% PAX3-GFP-positive somite cells with the combined condition

stages.name: Dermomyotome induction
stages.feeding: 3 days
actions: Treat somite cells with 5 uM CHIR99021 plus 10 ng/ml BMP4 for 3 days
For myogenic cells, continue the dermomyotome in 5 uM CHIR99021 for 30 days
stages.checkpoint: Dermomyotome gene expression at day 3 of this stage, with myogenic differentiation on extended CHIR99021 culture

tips: The CHIR99021 dose is stage-specific and non-monotonic: 10 uM is right for presomitic mesoderm and wrong (almost zero PAX3-GFP) for somite induction. This is the most important number in the protocol.
DLL1 sorting after presomitic mesoderm induction materially improves the somite step.
The paper's purpose was modelling fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, so patient-line comparisons are built into the system.
pitfalls: Carrying the presomitic CHIR99021 dose forward into the somite step destroys the induction.
Requires a FACS step and, for easy quantification, a PAX3 reporter.
Marker dynamics were measured in a reporter line; expect to re-titrate for other lines.
unverified: The CDM basal medium composition and the pre-culture medium are referenced to earlier work and were not verified here.

cell_types.notes: These are transient stages, so protocols are defined by timing as much as by reagents, and the CHIR99021 dose is both critical and stage-specific: 10 uM builds presomitic mesoderm in Nakajima 2018 but abolishes the subsequent somite step, where 5 uM is correct; Loh 2016 use 4 uM, then 3 uM, then Wnt inhibition on consecutive days. Always confirm the stage by marker, not by day count. Two sortable surface markers make this tractable: DLL1 for paraxial mesoderm and PDGFRA for sclerotome. For segmentation-clock work the relevant systems are 3D rather than monolayer: Matsuda et al. 2020 (Nature, PMID 32238941) recapitulate a roughly 5-hour human HES7 oscillation from hPSCs, Matsuda et al. 2020 (Science, PMID 32943519) show species-specific clock periods arise from differential biochemical reaction speeds, and Sanaki-Matsumiya et al. 2022 (Nat Commun, PMID 35484123) generate somitoids that bud epithelial somites periodically. Those papers' protocol parameters were not verified here.

cell_types.name: Kidney organoids
cell_types.summary: Three-dimensional tissues containing segmented nephrons (podocytes, proximal tubule, loop of Henle and distal tubule) and, depending on the protocol, collecting duct, stroma and endothelium, made by inducing posterior intermediate mesoderm and nephron progenitors then letting them self-organise. They are used to model polycystic kidney disease and congenital nephropathies, to test nephrotoxicity, and to study human nephrogenesis.
cell_types.maturation_note: Nephron progenitors appear by day 9 in the Morizane protocol (80-90% SIX2+) and renal vesicles around day 14, with segmented nephrons by day 21; organoids remain stable for at least three months. In the Takasato route the intermediate mesoderm takes 7 days, then aggregates develop for 11-18 days (day 7 to 25). Proximal tubule maturation remains the weak point in all protocols, and organoids stay fetal in character with no vasculature unless grafted or vascularised.

morphology.endpoint: A domed, 0.5 mm or larger aggregate on a transwell filter or in a round-bottom well, shot through with translucent convoluted tubules and lighter, denser glomerulus-like bodies; under higher power the tubules have clear lumens and the whole mass is surrounded by looser stroma.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Feeder-free hPSCs at the confluence the protocol specifies (40-50% for Takasato; carefully titrated for Morizane, where confluence at initiation is the single most important variable).

stages.label: Late primitive streak
stages.look: Loosely formed dense clusters of cells over a confluent sheet: in the Morizane protocol this is the cue to switch to activin A, and judging it correctly is the critical step.

stages.label: Nephron progenitors
stages.look: Dense monolayer with 80-90% SIX2-positive nuclei; ready to aggregate or continue in 2D.

stages.label: Renal vesicles
stages.look: Round polarised structures with clear lumens appear within the aggregate or monolayer; this is the point to withdraw CHIR99021.

stages.label: Segmented nephrons
stages.look: Convoluted tubules with distinguishable segments and glomerulus-like bodies; in Takasato organoids, collecting duct, renal interstitium and endothelium as well.

stages.label: Mature organoid
stages.look: Around 0.5 mm or larger, each organoid holding multiple nephron structures; tubules can be imaged live and take up labelled dextran.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Takasato 2016 note hPSCs should still be OCT4/NANOG positive on day 0 before CHIR99021 is added; it must be gone later.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Induced by the CHIR99021 phase; the balance of anterior versus posterior streak sets the collecting duct to nephron ratio.

markers.name: HOXD11
markers.note: The key posterior intermediate mesoderm check. Takasato 2016 stain day-7 cells for HOXD11 (posterior) alongside GATA3 (anterior) and treat HOXD11-negative cultures as a failed differentiation.

markers.name: WT1
markers.note: Positive with HOXD11 after the 3-day activin A step in Morizane 2017; later marks podocytes.

markers.name: SIX2
markers.note: The nephron progenitor readout: Morizane 2017 report 80-90% SIX2+SALL1+WT1+PAX2+EYA1+ cells at day 9.

markers.name: SALL1
markers.note: Co-expressed with SIX2 in true nephron progenitors.

markers.name: LHX1
markers.note: Morizane 2017 use LHX1 as the troubleshooting marker when renal vesicle structures fail to appear.

markers.name: NPHS1
markers.note: Marks the podocyte compartment of the organoid; with WT1 and PODXL the glomerular readout.

markers.name: PODXL
markers.note: Freedman 2015 report about 80% of LTL-positive organoids also containing PODXL-positive podocyte-like cells.

markers.name: LTL
markers.note: Proximal tubule brush-border lectin; Freedman 2015 report LTL-positive cells as about 25% of the total culture.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Distal epithelium; Morizane 2017 list the exact antibody. CDH1+GATA3+ cells indicate a collecting-duct-like population, which the Morizane protocol largely lacks and the Takasato protocol contains.

markers.name: GATA3
markers.note: Anterior intermediate mesoderm at day 7 in Takasato 2016 and the collecting duct lineage later; the CHIR99021 duration sets how much of this you get.

markers.name: HAVCR1
markers.note: Injury rather than identity marker: Freedman 2015 detected luminal KIM-1 in about 80% of organoids after cisplatin or gentamicin.

markers.name: TUBB3
markers.note: Off-target neural cells are a known contaminant of kidney organoids; Freedman 2015 screened for TUJ1 and intestinal markers.

functional_assays: Labelled dextran uptake into tubular lumens
Cisplatin or gentamicin nephrotoxicity with KIM-1 induction
Microinjection of tracers into tubular lumens
Whole-mount confocal imaging of nephron segmentation
Cystogenesis assay in PKD1/PKD2 mutant organoids
Transplantation and vascularisation in vivo
qc: HOXD11-positive (posterior intermediate mesoderm) at day 7 in the Takasato route; a HOXD11-negative day-7 culture should be restarted with adjusted density or CHIR99021 timing
SIX2-positive nephron progenitors at 80-90% by day 9 in the Morizane route
LHX1-positive renal vesicle stage before withdrawing CHIR99021
Segmented nephrons with distinguishable podocyte (NPHS1/PODXL), proximal (LTL) and distal (CDH1) compartments by day 21-25
Off-target neural (TUBB3) and intestinal markers scored and low

protocols.name: CHIR99021 then FGF9, aggregate on a transwell with a CHIR pulse (multi-lineage organoid)
protocols.principle: A CHIR99021 phase of adjustable length sets the anterior/posterior balance of the intermediate mesoderm, FGF9 with heparin then expands it; aggregating the day-7 cells on a transwell filter with a brief CHIR99021 pulse lets ureteric epithelium and metanephric mesenchyme interact, so nephrons, collecting duct, interstitium and endothelium all form in one organoid.

source.authors: Takasato M, Er PX, Chiu HS, Little MH
source.title: Generation of kidney organoids from human pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: High success rate, defined by the authors as organoids containing segmented nephrons with collecting duct, renal interstitium and endothelium; demonstrated for HES-3 hESCs and hiPSC lines
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs grown on MEF feeders then transferred to Matrigel for 2 days. Dissociate with TrypLE Select (3 min), pipetting no more than twice, and seed 375,000 cells into a Matrigel-coated 25 cm2 flask in MEF-conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/ml bFGF, i.e. 15 x 10^3 cells/cm2, overnight. Cells should be 40-50% confluent on day 0.

stages.name: Posterior primitive streak / intermediate mesoderm induction (CHIR phase)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt on, posteriorises the streak

stages.feeding: 4 ml APEL with 8 uM CHIR99021, refreshed every 2 days
actions: Check that cells are 40-50% confluent; adjust the seeding number if not
Add APEL medium containing 8 uM CHIR99021
Culture for 2-5 days, refreshing every 2 days
stages.checkpoint: The CHIR99021 duration sets the collecting duct to nephron ratio: shorter gives more anterior intermediate mesoderm, longer gives more posterior

stages.name: FGF9 phase
stages.feeding: 8 ml APEL with FGF9 and heparin, refreshed every 2 days until day 7
actions: Change to APEL with 200 ng/ml FGF9 and 1 ug/ml heparin
Use at least 0.32 ml of this medium per cm2
Refresh every 2 days to day 7
stages.checkpoint: Day-7 cells stain for GATA3 (anterior) and HOXD11 (posterior) intermediate mesoderm; HOXD11-negative means the differentiation failed

stages.name: Aggregation with a CHIR pulse

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: 1 h pulse on the transwell to trigger nephron formation

stages.feeding: 1.2 ml APEL with 5 uM CHIR99021 under the transwell for 1 h
actions: Dissociate and resuspend the day-7 cells in 3 ml APEL
Pellet, then place the pellets onto a 6-well transwell filter with minimal medium carryover
Aliquot 1.2 ml APEL containing 5 uM CHIR99021 beneath the filter and incubate 1 h at 37 C
stages.checkpoint: Pellets sitting intact on the filter at the air-liquid interface after the 1 h pulse

stages.name: Organoid growth with FGF9
stages.feeding: 1.2 ml APEL with FGF9 and heparin, refreshed every 2 days for 5 days
actions: After the 1 h pulse, replace the CHIR99021 medium with 1.2 ml APEL plus 200 ng/ml FGF9 and 1 ug/ml heparin
Culture the pellets 5 days, refreshing every 2 days
stages.checkpoint: Early nephron structures forming within the aggregate

stages.name: Factor-free maturation
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff APEL medium with no added factors
stages.feeding: APEL alone, refreshed every 2 days
actions: After 5 days with FGF9, change to APEL with no FGF9 or heparin
Culture a further 6-13 days (to day 18-25)
Proceed to whole-mount immunofluorescence or functional assays
stages.checkpoint: Organoids containing segmented nephrons plus collecting duct, renal interstitium and endothelium

materials: MEF feeders and MEF-conditioned hESC medium
Antibodies for whole-mount staining (GATA3, HOXD11, nephron segment markers)
tips: The CHIR99021 duration (2-5 days) is the main dial: use it to tune how much collecting duct versus nephron you get.
Use freshly thawed FGF9 and do not skimp on medium volume; both are listed as causes of failed intermediate mesoderm induction.
Check HOXD11 at day 7 before committing to aggregation; it is much cheaper than discovering the failure at day 25.
pitfalls: Cells coming off the plastic during the CHIR99021 phase means the seeding density was too low.
Inadequate FGF9 concentration or medium volume is the stated cause of inefficient intermediate mesoderm induction.
Carrying too much medium over when transferring pellets to the transwell disrupts the air-liquid interface.

protocols.name: High-efficiency nephron progenitors (80-90% SIX2+) then 2D or 3D nephron organoids
protocols.principle: Induce late primitive streak with a line-specific CHIR99021 dose (with or without a BMP inhibitor), then posterior intermediate mesoderm with activin A, then nephron progenitors with FGF9. A transient CHIR99021 plus FGF9 treatment converts the progenitors to renal vesicles, which self-organise into segmented nephrons in either 2D or 3D.

source.authors: Morizane R, Bonventre JV
source.title: Generation of nephron progenitor cells and kidney organoids from human pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: 80-90% SIX2+SALL1+WT1+PAX2+EYA1+ nephron progenitors within 9 days, with no sorting; 3D organoids about 0.5 mm in diameter containing multiple nephron structures
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs in ReproFF2 or StemFit Basic on 6-well plates coated with 1% LDEV-free hESC-qualified Geltrex, passaged with Accutase and plated with 10 uM Y-27632. Plating density at differentiation initiation strongly affects efficiency, so prepare several densities in parallel.

stages.name: Late primitive streak induction
stages.base_medium: Basic differentiation medium (Advanced RPMI 1640 with L-GlutaMAX)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.conc: 8 uM for H9 in ReproFF2; 10 uM for HDF-derived iPSCs
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt on, line-dependent dose

factors.name: Noggin
factors.conc: 5 ng/ml (used with 10 uM CHIR for the HDF line)
factors.role: BMP inhibitor; needed for some lines

stages.feeding: 500 ul per well, refreshed with the same CHIR concentration after 2 days
actions: Begin differentiation at the optimal plating density for your line
Treat with CHIR99021 (with or without noggin) for 2 days, refresh, and treat 2 more days
At about 96 h look for loosely formed dense cell clusters: that is the cue to move on
stages.checkpoint: Loosely formed dense clusters over the monolayer at about 96 h; if the sheet is still a homogeneous flat monolayer, feed again with the same CHIR medium rather than advancing

stages.name: Posterior intermediate mesoderm

factors.name: Activin A
factors.role: posterior intermediate mesoderm induction over 3 days (2 days can be tried if SIX2 induction is poor)

stages.feeding: No feeding usually needed over the 2-3 days
actions: Switch to activin A-containing medium once the dense clusters appear
Culture 2-3 days
If SIX2 induction is poor, test 2 days of activin A instead of 3
stages.checkpoint: WT1 and HOXD11 positive (posterior intermediate mesoderm) after 3 days of activin A

stages.name: Nephron progenitor induction
stages.feeding: 500 ul per well; usually no change needed, feed if the medium yellows
actions: Add basic differentiation medium with 10 ng/ml FGF9
Culture 1-2 days
stages.checkpoint: 80-90% SIX2-positive nephron progenitors at day 9 by immunocytochemistry

stages.name: Renal vesicle induction (2D or 3D)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: transient Wnt activation; converts progenitors to renal vesicles

stages.feeding: 2 days; for 3D, seed 100,000 cells/well in 200 ul into 96-well round-bottom ultra-low-attachment plates
actions: For 2D: replace the medium with 500 ul-1 ml of CHIR 3 uM plus FGF9 10 ng/ml for 2 days

For 3D: dissociate with Accutase (10-15 min), resuspend at 500,000 cells/ml in medium with CHIR 3 uM and FGF9 10 ng/ml and plate 100,000 cells per well of a 96-well round-bottom ultra-low-attachment plate
If round polarised structures with lumens already appear, shorten this step from 2 days to 1
stages.checkpoint: Round polarised structures with lumens (renal vesicles); LHX1 positive

stages.name: Nephron formation

factors.name: FGF9
factors.role: supports nephron formation after CHIR withdrawal

stages.feeding: 750 ul-1 ml for 2-3 days
actions: Withdraw CHIR99021 and continue with FGF9 alone for 2-3 days
If renal vesicles do not appear within 3 days, check LHX1; if LHX1 is positive, feed daily with FGF9 medium for 3 more days
stages.checkpoint: Renal vesicle structures clearly established before growth factors are withdrawn

stages.name: Growth-factor-free maturation
stages.base_medium: Basic differentiation medium with no growth factors
stages.feeding: 500-750 ul every 2-3 days
actions: Switch to basic differentiation medium with no growth factors
Feed every 2-3 days; organoids are stable for at least 3 months
Analyse nephron segments by immunocytochemistry (2D) or immunohistochemistry (3D) around day 21
stages.checkpoint: Segmented nephron structures at day 21; 3D organoids about 0.5 mm with multiple nephrons per well

materials: Anti-SIX2, anti-LHX1, anti-CDH1 (Abcam ab11512) and nephron segment antibodies
tips: The CHIR99021 dose and whether you need a BMP inhibitor are line- and medium-dependent: 8 uM for H9 in ReproFF2, 10 uM plus 5 ng/ml noggin for the HDF iPSC line.
Judging the day-4 morphology (loosely formed dense clusters) is the single most important decision in the protocol; feed again rather than advancing early.
If the induction rate of nephron progenitors is around 80%, 3D organoid formation is highly reproducible well to well.
The authors specify the exact CHIR99021 product because substitutes need re-titration.
pitfalls: Unlike the Takasato protocol, this route yields few CD31-positive endothelial or CDH1+GATA3+ collecting-duct-like cells, which matters if you need those lineages.
Interstitial cells in the organoid were not well characterised in the original study.
Some lines differentiate faster than expected and form renal vesicles spontaneously; shorten the CHIR step if so.
unverified: The activin A working concentration for the day 4-7 step is not stated in the portion of the protocol read here (the stock is prepared at 50 ug/ml); confirm against the paper's reagent setup before use.

protocols.name: Epiblast spheroids sandwiched in dilute Matrigel, then a high-dose CHIR99021 pulse
protocols.principle: Sandwiching hPSCs under dilute Matrigel produces isolated, lumen-containing epiblast spheroids; a 36 h high-dose CHIR99021 pulse then takes them through an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and back, so by about day 10 they fold and re-epithelialise into tubular kidney organoids. Simple enough to make CRISPR disease modelling (for example PKD1/PKD2 cystogenesis) practical.

source.authors: Freedman BS, Brooks CR, Lam AQ, Fu H, et al.
source.title: Modelling kidney disease with CRISPR-mutant kidney organoids derived from human pluripotent epiblast spheroids

protocols.efficiency: LTL-positive cells about 25% of the total culture; about 80% of LTL-positive organoids also contained CD31-positive endothelial and PODXL-positive podocyte-like cells
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained feeder-free on 3% reduced-growth-factor Geltrex for at least one passage in mTeSR1. Plate 60,000-120,000 H9 hPSCs per 1.9 cm2, enough to give scattered isolated spheroid colonies, then sandwich under dilute Matrigel.

stages.name: Epiblast spheroid formation (sandwiching)

factors.name: GelTrex overlay
factors.role: dilute matrix overlay that drives spheroid formation with a central lumen

stages.feeding: Overlay the day after plating, change medium after 24 h
actions: Plate 60,000-120,000 hPSCs per 1.9 cm2 on 3% Geltrex in mTeSR1
The following day replace the medium with 500 ul of 1.5% GelTrex in mTeSR1
Change the medium after 24 h and wait 48 h from sandwiching before inducing
stages.checkpoint: Scattered, isolated spheroid colonies with lumens

stages.name: CHIR99021 pulse
stages.base_medium: mTeSR1 (or RB minus insulin for the alternative schedule)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: high-dose GSK3 inhibition for 36 h (or 24 h in the alternative schedule)

factors.name: IWP2
factors.role: alternative schedule only: Wnt inhibition for 48 h after the CHIR pulse and a 48 h gap, mirroring 2D cardiomyocyte differentiation

stages.feeding: 36 h single treatment, or the staged alternative
actions: 48 h after sandwiching, treat the spheroids with 12 uM CHIR99021 for 36 h
Alternatively: 12 uM CHIR99021 in RB minus insulin for 24 h, RBNI for 48 h, 5 uM IWP2 for 48 h, RBNI for 48 h
stages.checkpoint: Spheroid cells undergoing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition

stages.name: Tubular organoid formation and maturation
stages.base_medium: RB: Advanced RPMI with 1x GlutaMAX and 1x B27 supplement
stages.feeding: RB replaced every 3 days
actions: Change to RB medium after the CHIR pulse and replace every 3 days
Expect the monolayer to aggregate into folds by about day 10 and undergo mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition into convoluted translucent tubular organoids
Assay dextran uptake, KIM-1 induction after cisplatin or gentamicin, or cyst formation in PKD mutants
stages.checkpoint: Tubular organoids with LTL-positive proximal tubule; about 80% also containing CD31-positive endothelium and PODXL-positive podocyte-like cells

tips: The sandwich step is what makes the organoids reproducible: plate sparsely enough to get isolated spheroids rather than a confluent sheet.
Cysts form in PKD1/PKD2 knockout organoids, which is the main published application; they appear over weeks (a representative cyst is shown at day 58).
Rhodamine dextran localises to tubular lumens within 2-4 h and persists through a 24 h washout, which is a quick functional check.
pitfalls: LTL-positive cells are only about a quarter of the culture, so this protocol trades purity for simplicity and genetic tractability.
Two induction schedules are published (36 h CHIR alone, or the staged CHIR/IWP2 version); do not mix them.
Organoid tubules are fetal and non-vascularised in vitro, as in all of these protocols.

cell_types.notes: The three protocols are genuinely different products. Takasato organoids contain nephrons plus collecting duct, interstitium and endothelium and let you tune the collecting duct to nephron ratio with the length of the CHIR99021 phase; Morizane organoids are nephron-focused with 80-90% SIX2-positive progenitors but few collecting-duct or endothelial cells; Freedman organoids are the simplest and most genetically tractable but only about 25% of the culture is proximal tubule. Starting cell density and confluence at induction dominate reproducibility in all three, and the CHIR99021 dose is line-dependent (8 uM for H9 versus 10 uM plus noggin for an HDF iPSC line in Morizane 2017). All three give fetal, non-vascularised tissue; proximal tubule maturity and off-target neural cells remain the main limitations.

cell_types.name: Podocytes
cell_types.summary: Large, arborised glomerular epithelial cells with interdigitating foot processes that express nephrin, podocin and synaptopodin and form the filtration barrier with glomerular endothelium. iPSC-derived podocytes are used to model nephrotic syndrome and APOL1-associated kidney disease, to study filtration on glomerulus-on-a-chip devices, and for nephrotoxicity testing.
cell_types.maturation_note: Musah's route takes 2 days to mesoderm, a minimum of 14 days to intermediate mesoderm and 4-5 days of podocyte induction, so about three weeks in total, and reaches over 90% efficiency. The one-step Rauch protocol gives podocyte-like cells in 10 days of differentiation medium followed by 10 days of maintenance medium. Foot processes and interdigitations are the slowest feature to appear and depend strongly on cell density and on being on laminin.

morphology.endpoint: Very large, flat, polygonal to stellate cells with long arborised processes that interdigitate with their neighbours; nuclei are large and the cells cover far more area than the progenitors they came from.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Round colonies with defined boundaries on Matrigel in mTeSR, 3-4 days post-passage and about 70% confluent.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: An even monolayer on laminin-511-E8 after two days of activin A, CHIR99021 and ROCK inhibitor.

stages.label: Intermediate mesoderm
stages.look: A confluent, fairly uniform epithelial-looking sheet that can be passaged for up to a month or cryopreserved.

stages.label: Podocytes
stages.look: Cells enlarge dramatically and develop branched processes that contact neighbouring cells; nephrin and podocin staining outlines the cell borders.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent; Rauch 2018 track OCT4 and SOX2 transcripts falling across the 17-day differentiation.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Second exit-from-pluripotency marker in the Rauch time course.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Induced over the first two days of activin A plus CHIR99021 on laminin in the Musah route.

markers.name: PAX2
markers.note: Intermediate mesoderm and renal progenitor marker during the 14-day BMP7/CHIR99021 phase.

markers.name: WT1
markers.note: Podocyte transcription factor; Musah 2018 stain for nephrin, WT1 and podocin together as the podocyte panel.

markers.name: NPHS1
markers.note: Slit diaphragm protein and the key specificity marker; Musah 2018 report over 90% efficiency using this panel.

markers.name: NPHS2
markers.note: Slit diaphragm protein; co-stained with nephrin and WT1.

markers.name: SYNPO
markers.note: Foot process cytoskeletal marker; Rauch 2018 follow SYNPO transcript across days 1, 3, 6, 9, 13 and 17.

markers.name: PODXL
markers.note: Apical surface sialoprotein of podocytes; widely used for flow quantification.

markers.name: MAFB
markers.note: Podocyte transcription factor commonly included alongside WT1.

markers.name: SYNPO2
markers.note: Secondary cytoskeletal readout of maturity.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Podocytes are not E-cadherin-high epithelium; strong CDH1 suggests tubular drift.

markers.name: LTL
markers.note: Proximal tubule contamination, the usual off-target when the protocol slips towards general nephron fate.

markers.name: TUBB3
