protocols.name: Laminin-511-E8 with activin A/CHIR, BMP7/CHIR, then BMP7/activin A/VEGF/retinoic acid/CHIR
protocols.principle: Culture on a laminin-511-E8 fragment (the podocyte's own basement membrane ligand) and step the cells through mesoderm and intermediate mesoderm, then apply a five-component podocyte induction medium. The matrix is as important as the soluble factors, and the result is mature podocytes at over 90% efficiency, suitable for a glomerulus-on-a-chip.

source.authors: Musah S, Dimitrakakis N, Camacho DM, Church GM, Ingber DE
source.title: Directed differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells into mature kidney podocytes and establishment of a glomerulus chip

protocols.start_requirements: Human iPS or ES cells adapted to feeder-free culture in mTeSR on Matrigel-coated plates, used 3-4 days after passaging at about 70% confluency and in the mitotic phase, with any spontaneously differentiated cells scraped away first. All 2D differentiation is done in 12-well plates on laminin-511-E8 coated at 5 ug/ml (700 ul per well).

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with GlutaMAX and 1x B27 serum-free supplement

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; survival of the replated single cells

stages.feeding: Refresh the medium the next day; 2 days total
actions: Rinse iPSCs three times with pre-warmed DMEM/F12 and dissociate with enzyme-free dissociation buffer for about 10 min at 37 C
Scrape gently, pipette to individualise the cells and pellet
Resuspend in mesoderm induction medium and plate 1 ml per well of a laminin-511-E8-coated 12-well plate
Refresh the medium the next day and culture 2 days in total
stages.checkpoint: Even mesoderm monolayer at day 2

stages.name: Intermediate mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with GlutaMAX and 1x B27 serum-free supplement
stages.feeding: 1 ml per well of a 12-well plate, refreshed daily for at least 14 days
actions: Replace the mesoderm medium with intermediate mesoderm medium
Refresh daily; if the medium turns yellow, increase the volume
Culture 14 days; the cells can be passaged for up to a month or cryopreserved at this stage
stages.checkpoint: Confluent intermediate mesoderm culture after 14 days (about 100% confluent before passaging)

stages.name: Podocyte induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with GlutaMAX and 1x B27 serum-free supplement

factors.name: All-trans retinoic acid
factors.role: podocyte specification; the medium must be protected from light

stages.feeding: Refresh daily for 4-5 days
actions: Rinse the intermediate mesoderm cells three times with DMEM/F12 and dissociate with 0.05% trypsin-EDTA (0.5 ml per well, about 3 min at 37 C)
Neutralise with DMEM/F12 plus 10% FBS, avoiding clumps larger than 200 um
Centrifuge 5 min at 201 x g and replate at a 1:4 split ratio onto fresh laminin-511-E8 in podocyte induction medium
Refresh daily for 4-5 days, keeping the retinoic acid-containing medium in the dark
stages.checkpoint: Nephrin, WT1 and podocin positive with arborised, interdigitating morphology after 4-5 days; over 90% efficiency by flow

materials: iMatrix-511 laminin-E8 fragment (Iwai N-892012) at 5 ug/ml
Recombinant human laminin-511 (BioLamina LN511-02) at 50 ug/ml for chips
Microfluidic chip with side vacuum chambers (optional)
tips: Laminin-511-E8 is not interchangeable with Matrigel here; the matrix is part of the specification.
Lot-test CHIR99021: the authors explicitly report quality differences between suppliers and lots.
Protect the retinoic acid medium from light, and refresh daily because the cells deplete the factors quickly.
Intermediate mesoderm cells can be banked, so one differentiation can supply many podocyte experiments.
On the chip, cyclic mechanical strain applied through the side vacuum chambers mimics glomerular pulsation and improves the barrier.
pitfalls: Start from mitotic, roughly 70%-confluent iPSCs; over-confluent or partly differentiated starting cultures fail.
Clumps larger than 200 um at the podocyte replating step do not spread and will not form interdigitations.
The PDMS chip can absorb small hydrophobic molecules, which limits some drug studies (a limitation the authors state).
This protocol makes only podocytes; it is not a route to other kidney cell types.

protocols.name: One-step podocyte differentiation: activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid in low serum
protocols.principle: A single differentiation medium containing activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid applied directly to seeded iPSCs for ten days, followed by ten days in factor-free maintenance medium, yields podocyte-like cells. Initial and seeding cell densities, and how the plate is handled when seeding, determine whether foot processes and interdigitations form.

source.authors: Rauch C, Feifel E, Kern G, Murphy C, et al.
source.title: Differentiation of human iPSCs into functional podocytes

protocols.start_requirements: Pre-cultures of undifferentiated iPSCs plated at 50,000-100,000, 200,000 or 400,000 cells/cm2 and grown 4 days, then passaged with Accutase to single cells and seeded on Geltrex-coated plates at 9,000, 15,000 or 40,000 cells/cm2 for differentiation. Seed in half the recommended medium volume, rock the plate gently back-and-forth and left-right rather than swirling, and add the rest of the medium after 5 h once cells have attached.

stages.name: Podocyte differentiation (medium M1)
stages.base_medium: DMEM/Ham's F-12 with 1.25% FBS, 100 uM non-essential amino acids, 100 U/ml penicillin and 0.1 mg/ml streptomycin
stages.feeding: ROCK inhibitor removed at 24 h by feeding with M1; then fed every 2-3 days for 10 days
actions: Seed undifferentiated iPSCs directly into medium M1 with 5 uM Y-27632
After 24 h feed with M1 to remove the ROCK inhibitor
Maintain in M1, feeding every 2-3 days, for 10 days
stages.checkpoint: Synaptopodin transcript rising across days 1, 3, 6 and 9 with OCT4 and SOX2 falling

stages.name: Maintenance (medium M2)
stages.base_medium: DMEM/Ham's F-12 with 2.5% FBS, 100 uM non-essential amino acids, 100 U/ml penicillin and 0.1 mg/ml streptomycin
stages.feeding: Medium changed every 48 h for 10 days
actions: Switch to factor-free medium M2 at day 10
Change medium every 48 h for a further 10 days
stages.checkpoint: Podocyte-like cells with foot processes and interdigitations between neighbouring cells at day 17-20

tips: The authors single out seeding and handling technique: half-volume seeding, gentle back-and-forth and left-right rocking rather than swirling, and adding the remaining medium after 5 h, all to avoid an uneven concentric cell distribution.
It is a one-step protocol with no passaging, which makes it quick and cheap when you only need podocyte-like cells.
The 20-day time course with qPCR at days 1, 3, 6, 9, 13 and 17 published in the paper is a useful benchmark.
pitfalls: Both the density of the undifferentiated pre-culture and the seeding density of the differentiation culture must be controlled; the paper devotes a section to this.
Uneven concentric distribution in multiwell plates prevents proper foot process and interdigitation formation.
No purity percentage is reported, so this route is harder to benchmark than the Musah protocol.
unverified: No differentiation efficiency or purity percentage is reported.

protocols.name: Embryoid-body route with activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid
protocols.principle: The earliest hiPSC podocyte protocol: suspend colony fragments as embryoid bodies in a low-serum medium containing activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid for three days, then plate them on gelatin in the same medium for a further week, giving podocytes at about day 10 that can be maintained without the factors.

source.authors: Song B, Smink AM, Jones CV, Callaghan JM, et al.
source.title: The directed differentiation of human iPS cells into kidney podocytes

protocols.start_requirements: iPSC colonies (in this paper reprogrammed from normal human kidney mesangial cells) cut mechanically into similarly sized pieces.

stages.name: Embryoid body induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with 2.5% FBS, 100 uM non-essential amino acids and 100 uM beta-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: 3 days in ultra-low-cluster 6-well plates
actions: Cut iPSC colonies mechanically into similarly sized pieces
Culture in ultra-low-cluster 6-well plates in the differentiation medium for 3 days
stages.checkpoint: Embryoid bodies formed and ready to plate

stages.name: Adherent podocyte differentiation
stages.base_medium: Same differentiation medium (DMEM/F12 with 2.5% FBS, NEAA, beta-mercaptoethanol)
stages.feeding: 7-8 days in the same medium before sub-passaging
actions: Transfer the embryoid bodies to 0.1% gelatin pre-coated 10 cm dishes
Culture a further 7-8 days in the same medium
At day 10 fix in 2.5% glutaraldehyde in cacodylate buffer for scanning electron microscopy, or sub-passage for characterisation
For long-term maintenance, continue in DMEM/F12 without activin A, BMP7 or retinoic acid
stages.checkpoint: Podocyte morphology by SEM at day 10, with podocin, synaptopodin and nephrin expression; cells keep their morphology and function in factor-free medium

materials: Glutaraldehyde and cacodylate buffer for SEM
tips: The activin A, BMP7 and retinoic acid combination established here is the basis of the later Rauch and Musah media, which is why the three protocols look related.
Podocytes keep their morphology and function after the factors are withdrawn, so you do not need to maintain them on expensive medium.
The paper compares the iPSC podocytes directly with primary human podocytes isolated by glomerular sieving, a good benchmark design.
pitfalls: Embryoid-body routes are inherently heterogeneous: Musah 2018 cite exactly this as the reason EB-based podocyte differentiation is inefficient.
No purity figure is given, so quantification needs to be added by the user.
Mechanical cutting of colonies is operator-dependent and hard to standardise.
unverified: No differentiation efficiency or purity percentage is reported.

cell_types.notes: Efficiency differs enormously between routes and most of the difference comes from the matrix and from heterogeneity. Musah et al. report over 90% mature podocytes on laminin-511-E8 and explicitly attribute part of that to the matrix, contrasting it with embryoid-body routes (Song 2012) and with organoids, where podocytes are only one component. The one-step Rauch protocol is quick but gives no purity number and is highly sensitive to seeding density and even to how the plate is rocked. Whichever route you use, judge success on arborised morphology and interdigitating processes as well as on nephrin/podocin/WT1 staining: marker-positive flat cells are not functional podocytes. Note also that CHIR99021 lots vary enough to change the outcome (a caution the Musah protocol makes explicitly).

cell_types.name: Ureteric bud / collecting duct organoids
cell_types.summary: The branching epithelium that forms the collecting duct system and ureter, derived through anterior (not posterior) intermediate mesoderm and nephric duct rather than through nephron progenitors. hPSC-derived ureteric bud organoids branch in culture, can be expanded, differentiate to principal and intercalated collecting duct cells, and can be recombined with nephron progenitors to build higher-order kidney tissue; they also model ADPKD cystogenesis and lower urinary tract disorders.
cell_types.maturation_note: The Osafune-lab route reaches nephric duct in about 6 days (16-28 h anterior primitive streak, 3 days anterior intermediate mesoderm, 2 days nephric duct elongation), epithelialises the aggregate in 2 days and gives a branching ureteric bud organoid by day 6 of 3D culture, so under two weeks to a branching organoid. Tips can be separated and reconstituted repeatedly (3-4 times), and collecting duct progenitors take a further 7 days in 2D or 14 days in 3D. Zeng 2021 organoids expand for months, with human collecting duct differentiation taking 14 days.

morphology.endpoint: A translucent epithelial organoid with a hollow trunk and multiple rounded buds or tips at its periphery, visibly branching over days; sections show a single-layered CK8/RET-positive epithelium around a lumen.

stages.label: Anterior primitive streak
stages.look: After 16-28 h in activin A plus CHIR99021 the monolayer is BRACHYURY-positive; residual SOX2-positive hPSCs mean the induction was too short.

stages.label: Anterior intermediate mesoderm
stages.look: Dense monolayer co-expressing GATA3, LHX1 and PAX2; the cells are replated at 1 x 10^5 cells/cm2 partway through.

stages.label: Nephric duct
stages.look: Epithelial-looking sheet positive for RET and GATA3; when induction is patchy the positive cells form islands rather than a continuous sheet.

stages.label: Nephric duct aggregate
stages.look: One aggregate per well of a 96-well M-bottom plate, with a bright duct core and a looser halo of unwanted cells that is pipetted away.

stages.label: Branching ureteric bud organoid
stages.look: Floating organoid with distinct budding tips; laminin and ezrin outline the epithelium, with RET concentrated in the tips.

stages.label: Collecting duct
stages.look: Tip-derived colonies or reconstituted organoids expressing collecting duct markers after further differentiation.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Ryosaka 2022 co-stain day-0 anterior primitive streak cells for BRACHYURY and SOX2; remaining SOX2-positive cells mark incomplete induction.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: The 16-28 h readout; Zeng 2021 see mesendodermal T expression in most cells by day 3 of their schedule.

markers.name: GATA3
markers.stage_label: Anterior intermediate mesoderm and nephric duct
markers.note: The anterior intermediate mesoderm marker that distinguishes this lineage from the posterior (nephron) lineage; co-expressed with LHX1 and PAX2 at day 3.

markers.name: LHX1
markers.note: Part of the GATA3/LHX1/PAX2 triple stain at 72 h of anterior intermediate mesoderm induction.

markers.name: PAX2
markers.note: Zeng 2021 used a PAX2-mCherry knock-in reporter to purify precursors, and showed KIT-positive sorting enriches the same PAX2-positive population.

markers.name: RET
markers.note: The tip progenitor marker and the GDNF receptor; Zeng 2021 showed RET knockout blocks branching, and used an anti-RET extracellular-domain antibody to isolate human tip cells.

markers.name: WNT11
markers.note: Tip-restricted; Zeng 2021 built a WNT11-GFP reporter alongside PAX2-mCherry.

markers.name: KRT8
markers.note: Epithelial identity of the bud; Ryosaka 2022 stain cryosections for CK8 with RET.

markers.name: KIT
markers.note: The reporter-free sorting handle in Zeng 2021: 36.1% KIT-positive cells in a hESC line, 55.4% in H1 and 43.9% in SOX9-GFP hiPSCs after 7 days of differentiation.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Zeng 2021 purified SOX9-GFP-positive precursors on day 7 from a reporter hiPSC line.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Used with RET in whole-mount staining of reconstituted organoids.

markers.name: AQP2
markers.note: Principal cell marker and one of the two screening endpoints Zeng 2021 used to find their collecting duct differentiation medium.

markers.name: FOXI1
markers.note: Intercalated cell marker; the second screening endpoint in Zeng 2021.

markers.name: SIX2
markers.note: Should be absent: nephron progenitors come from posterior intermediate mesoderm and their presence means the anterior patterning drifted.

functional_assays: Branching morphogenesis quantified over days of live imaging
Serial tip separation and organoid reconstitution (3-4 rounds)
Recombination with nephron progenitor aggregates to build higher-order kidney tissue
RET or GDNF knockout to test branching dependence
Cystogenesis in ADPKD (PKD1/PKD2) collecting duct organoids
AQP2 and FOXI1 induction as collecting duct differentiation readouts
qc: BRACHYURY-positive and SOX2-negative at the end of the anterior primitive streak step
GATA3, LHX1 and PAX2 co-expression at 72 h of anterior intermediate mesoderm induction, as a continuous sheet rather than islands
RET and GATA3 co-expression after nephric duct elongation
Laminin and ezrin showing a polarised single-layered epithelium, with RET and CK8 positive, in day-7 organoids
SIX2 absent (confirming the anterior, not posterior, intermediate mesoderm lineage)

protocols.name: Osafune-lab iUB organoids: anterior primitive streak, anterior intermediate mesoderm, nephric duct, then 3D budding
protocols.principle: The ureteric bud arises from anterior rather than posterior intermediate mesoderm, so the first step is an anterior primitive streak induction with activin A and low CHIR99021 followed by retinoid, BMP and TGF-beta manipulation with FGF8. Nephric duct cells are then aggregated, epithelialised and cultured in a Matrigel-containing medium with GDNF, where they bud and branch; tips can be separated and reconstituted indefinitely.

source.authors: Ryosaka M, Mae SI, Osafune K
source.title: Protocol for the generation and expansion of human iPS cell-derived ureteric bud organoids

protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs (for example 1231A3, 1383D2) with 1 day of pre-differentiation in StemFit AK02N before the anterior primitive streak step; two wells of a 4-well plate per standard experiment.

stages.name: Anterior primitive streak induction

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; low-dose Wnt keeps the streak anterior

stages.feeding: 500 ul APS medium per well, made fresh, for 16-28 h
actions: After 1 day of pre-differentiation in StemFit AK02N, wash with 500 ul PBS
Add 500 ul freshly made APS medium per well
Incubate 16-28 h, optimising the time for your line
stages.checkpoint: BRACHYURY-positive, SOX2-negative cells; SOX2-positive cells mean the induction was too short

stages.name: Anterior intermediate mesoderm induction

factors.name: TTNPB
factors.role: retinoic acid receptor agonist; anteriorises the intermediate mesoderm

stages.feeding: 1 ml AIM medium per well for 2 days without a change, then replate and give 24 h more
actions: Wash with 500 ul PBS and add 1 ml AIM medium per well; incubate 2 days without changing the medium
Coat 24-well plates with 300 ul undiluted Geltrex for 1 h at 37 C
Dissociate with 300 ul Accutase for exactly 3 min at 37 C and pipette about ten times
Stop with DMEM/10% FBS, centrifuge 200 x g for 5 min
Replate at 1.0 x 10^5 cells/cm2 in Geltrex-coated 24-well plates in 500 ul AIM medium with 10 uM Y-27632 and incubate 24 h
stages.checkpoint: GATA3, LHX1 and PAX2 co-expression at 72 h of AIM induction

stages.name: Nephric duct elongation

factors.name: GDNF
factors.role: RET ligand; nephric duct and ureteric bud signal

stages.feeding: 1 ml ND medium per well of a 24-well plate for 2 days without a change
actions: Wash the AIM cells with 500 ul PBS
Add 1 ml ND medium per well and incubate 2 days without changing the medium
stages.checkpoint: RET and GATA3 co-expressing nephric duct cells

stages.name: Nephric duct epithelialisation (aggregation)
stages.base_medium: Essential 6 medium with the ND factor set
stages.feeding: 100 ul ND medium per well of a low-attachment M-bottom 96-well plate for 2 days
actions: Dissociate the ND cells with Accutase (3 min) and pipette about ten times
Seed 1 x 10^4 cells per well in 100 ul ND medium plus 10 uM Y-27632 in low-attachment M-bottom 96-well plates
Optionally centrifuge the plate at 200 x g for 2 min to help aggregation
Incubate 2 days; one aggregate forms per well
stages.checkpoint: One nephric duct aggregate per well, with a halo of unwanted non-ureteric cells

stages.name: iUB organoid induction

factors.name: LDN193189
factors.role: BMP inhibition (ten times the ND concentration)

stages.feeding: 100 ul UB organoid medium per well, changed every 2 days for 6 days
actions: Separate the unwanted cells from the aggregate by pipetting 10-20 times with a 10 or 200 ul pipette (not more than 30 times, which breaks the aggregate)
Aspirate the ND medium and add 100 ul UB organoid medium per well
Incubate 6 days, changing the medium every 2 days
stages.checkpoint: Floating day-6 iUB organoid with clear budding regions; laminin/ezrin-polarised epithelium and CK8/RET-positive cryosections at day 7

stages.name: Optional: tip separation and reconstitution
stages.base_medium: Essential 6 medium with 2% Matrigel (UB organoid medium, or the reconstituted version with R-spondin 1 and Afamin/Wnt3a conditioned medium)

factors.name: R-spondin 1
factors.role: Wnt agonist in the reconstituted organoid medium

factors.name: Afamin/Wnt3a conditioned medium
factors.role: Wnt source in the reconstituted organoid medium

stages.feeding: 100 ul per well, changed every 2 days for 14 days
actions: Move day-6 iUB organoids into a 35 mm dish with 2 ml Essential 6 medium
Separate tip regions with two 22G needles under a stereomicroscope
Place one tip per well of a low-attachment M-bottom 96-well plate with 100 ul UB organoid medium
Incubate 14 days, changing medium every 2 days; the process can be repeated 3-4 times per tip
stages.checkpoint: Day-14 reconstituted organoid positive for RET and E-cadherin by 3D whole-mount staining

tips: Use M-bottom (spindle-shaped) 96-well plates, not U-bottom: the authors state U-bottom plates make it hard to form and observe the aggregates.
Nephric duct cells can be cryopreserved at up to 2 x 10^6 cells/ml in STEMCELL BANKER, which breaks the protocol into manageable sessions.
The LDN193189 concentration increases tenfold (0.1 uM to 1 uM) when you move from nephric duct to organoid medium; this is easy to miss.
Pipette the aggregate 10-20 times to remove unwanted cells, and never more than 30, or budding is reduced.
pitfalls: Accutase exposure beyond 3 min reduces viability at every dissociation step.
If the GATA3/PAX2-positive cells form islands rather than a sheet, the nephric duct induction rate is too low and the anterior primitive streak step must be re-optimised.
Reduced or thickened budding regions in day-6 organoids indicate a low induction rate (the paper's troubleshooting item 3).
Every medium must be made fresh for each use.
unverified: No numeric induction efficiency or purity percentage is given in this protocol paper.

protocols.name: Expandable iUB organoids from KIT-sorted precursors, with a collecting duct differentiation medium
protocols.principle: A 7-day directed differentiation generates ureteric bud precursors that can be purified on the surface marker KIT (CD117) without any reporter, then expanded for months as branching organoids in a ureteric bud culture medium; a separately screened differentiation medium converts them to a patterned collecting duct organoid containing principal and intercalated cells.

source.authors: Zeng Z, Huang B, Parvez RK, Li Y, et al.
source.title: Generation of patterned kidney organoids that recapitulate the adult kidney collecting duct system from expandable ureteric bud progenitors

protocols.efficiency: KIT-positive cells at day 7: 36.1% (WNT11-GFP/PAX2-mCherry hESC), 55.4% (H1 hESC) and 43.9% (SOX9-GFP hiPSC); about 30% of single mouse ureteric bud cells self-organised at clonal density
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs pre-treated with 10 uM Y-27632 in mTeSR1 for 1 h, dissociated to single cells with Accumax, and 60,000-80,000 cells seeded per Matrigel-coated 12-well plate in 1 ml mTeSR1 with either 10 uM Y-27632 (original protocol) or 1x CloneR (refined protocol). Seeding number needs optimising per line.

stages.name: Mesendoderm (ME) stage

factors.name: ME stage medium components
factors.role: mesendoderm induction (composition in the paper's supplementary methods)

stages.feeding: 1 ml pre-warmed ME stage medium added slowly on day 1, for 48 h
actions: 24 h after seeding (day 1), remove the mTeSR1 and slowly add 1 ml ME stage medium
Culture 48 h
stages.checkpoint: Mesendoderm marker T expressed in most cells on day 3

stages.name: UB-I stage

factors.name: UB-I stage medium components
factors.role: first ureteric bud patterning step (composition in the supplementary methods)

stages.feeding: 1 ml on day 3, refreshed on day 4
actions: On day 3 replace with 1 ml UB-I medium
On day 4 refresh with fresh UB-I medium
stages.checkpoint: Progression towards the ureteric bud lineage

stages.name: UB-II stage

factors.name: UB-II stage medium components
factors.role: second ureteric bud patterning step (composition in the supplementary methods)

stages.feeding: 1.5-2 ml on day 5, refreshed on day 6
actions: On day 5 replace with 1.5-2 ml UB-II medium
On day 6 refresh
stages.checkpoint: Compact colonies that are GATA3+/SOX9+/PAX2+/PAX8+/KIT+/KRT8+ on day 7

stages.name: Precursor purification
stages.feeding: 30 min on ice with mixing every 10 min
actions: Dissociate the day-7 culture with Accumax
For non-reporter lines, stain with PE anti-CD117 at 1:200 for 30 min on ice
Add DAPI at 1:2000, filter through a 40 um strainer and sort KIT-positive cells (or mCherry/GFP-positive cells for reporter lines)
stages.checkpoint: KIT-positive fraction of 36-55% depending on the line; sorted cells express PAX2, GATA3 and LHX1

stages.name: iUB organoid expansion
stages.base_medium: hUBCM (human ureteric bud culture medium) or hUBCM-v2, based on the hBI14 base medium

factors.name: hUBCM/hUBCM-v2 components
factors.role: expansion of ureteric bud progenitors as branching organoids (composition in the supplementary methods)

stages.feeding: Medium renewed every 2 days; organoids passaged every 6-10 days depending on size, manually or as single cells
actions: Culture the sorted precursors in hUBCM or hUBCM-v2
Renew medium every 2 days and passage every 6-10 days
Expand until the culture is stable (at least 25 days post-FACS) and organoids reach at least 900 um diameter
Check gene expression stability at 33, 49 and 66 days against human fetal kidney
stages.checkpoint: Stably branching organoids at least 900 um across with maintained SOX9-GFP or WNT11-GFP expression

stages.name: Collecting duct differentiation
stages.base_medium: hCDDM (human collecting duct differentiation medium), screened from the hBI base with FGF9 and Y-27632 plus added factors including BMP7 and pathway inhibitors

factors.name: hCDDM components (including FGF9, Y-27632 and BMP7)
factors.role: induces AQP2 (principal cell) and FOXI1 (intercalated cell) programmes

stages.feeding: 150 ul hCDDM per organoid, changed every 2 days (or daily if the medium turns yellow) for 14 days
actions: Once expansion is stable and organoids are at least 900 um, wash with 150 ul PBS
Add 150 ul hCDDM to start differentiation (day 0 of CD differentiation)
Culture 14 days, changing medium every 2 days
Harvest at day 14 for analysis
stages.checkpoint: AQP2-positive principal cells and FOXI1-positive intercalated cells in the patterned collecting duct organoid

materials: Lentiviral CRISPR reagents (for RET knockout experiments)
tips: KIT (CD117) sorting is the practical breakthrough here: it removes the need for a reporter line and works across hESC and hiPSC lines.
Wait for expansion to stabilise (at least 25 days post-FACS, organoids at least 900 um) before starting collecting duct differentiation.
Gene expression stayed stable at 33, 49 and 66 days of culture, so these organoids genuinely expand rather than drift.
The same system supports recombination with nephron progenitor aggregates to build an engineered kidney precursor at an air-liquid interface.
pitfalls: The exact media formulations are in the supplementary methods, so you cannot run this protocol from the main text alone.
Seeding number must be optimised per line (60,000-80,000 cells per 12-well is only a starting point).
GDNF/RET signalling is essential: RET knockout abolishes branching, so check RET expression if organoids stop branching.

cell_types.notes: The crucial distinction is anterior versus posterior intermediate mesoderm: ureteric bud and collecting duct come from the anterior lineage (GATA3/LHX1/PAX2, then RET), whereas nephron progenitors (SIX2) come from the posterior lineage, which is why most nephron organoid protocols contain little or no collecting duct. In the Takasato protocol the length of the CHIR99021 phase shifts the balance between the two. Two practical routes exist for a dedicated ureteric bud: the Osafune-lab iUB organoid (Mae et al. 2018, Biochem Biophys Res Commun, PMID 29158085, with the step-by-step version in Ryosaka et al. 2022, and an ADPKD collecting duct application in Mae et al. 2023, Cell Rep, PMID 38039961), and the expandable KIT-sorted organoid of Zeng et al. 2021, which can be grown for months and then differentiated to a patterned collecting duct. Both depend on GDNF/RET signalling, and RET loss abolishes branching. Taguchi and Nishinakamura 2017 established the reassembly strategy that makes higher-order kidney tissue possible, but its protocol parameters are behind a paywall.
